sub_service: Lifting of municipal solid waste from roads / streets
problem_type: Uncollected garbage / solid waste not lifted from a road or street
department: Urban Local Body (Municipal Corporation / Municipality / NAC) -- Solid Waste Management Section, under the Directorate of Municipal Administration, Housing & Urban Development Department, Government of Odisha
description: Citizens can lodge a complaint about municipal solid waste not being lifted from a road or street. The complaint can be registered online (through a grievance redressal website or app) or manually at the ULB's solid waste management division or with the concerned ward officer/sanitary inspector. Identity proof of the complainant is required at registration.
procedure: Online: (1) Visit the applicable grievance redressal website (e.g. www.cmgcorissa.gov.in, www.ulborissa.gov.in, or a city-specific portal such as www.mycitymypride.org for Bhubaneswar Municipal Corporation) or call the toll-free grievance number, or use the solid waste management mobile app, if available. (2) Lodge a grievance stating the locality/ward and the complainant's phone number. (3) Collect the acknowledgement receipt. (4) Track the status of the complaint online. Manual: (1) Visit the solid waste management division of the concerned ULB, or contact the concerned ward officer/sanitary inspector directly. (2) Lodge a grievance stating the locality/ward and the complainant's phone number. (3) Collect an acknowledgement receipt. (4) Follow up on the status of the complaint with the same office.
sla: 3 days process time limit, per the HUDD Citizen's Charter.
complaint_channel: Online grievance portal (ULB or city-specific, e.g. www.cmgcorissa.gov.in, www.ulborissa.gov.in, www.mycitymypride.org for BMC)
Toll-free grievance number (city-specific, not uniformly listed in the source document)
Mobile application for solid waste management, where available
In person at the ULB's solid waste management division or with the concerned ward sanitary inspector
contact_information: Concerned ward Sanitary Inspector or the ULB's Solid Waste Management division; city-specific toll-free numbers and portals vary by ULB and are not individually listed in the source document.
escalation_procedure: If the service is not delivered within the stated process time limit, escalate per HUDD's Citizen's Charter grievance escalation matrix. For Municipal Corporations: Level 1 - Additional Municipal Commissioner / Executive Officer (7 days response time); Level 2 - Municipal Commissioner (7 days response time); Level 3 - Directorate of Municipal Administration, DMA (15 days response time); Level 4 - Commissioner-cum-Secretary, Housing & Urban Development Department (30 days response time). For Municipalities/NACs: Level 1 - City Manager (7 days response time); Level 2 - Section Head (7 days response time); Level 3 - Executive Officer (7 days response time); Level 4 - Directorate of Municipal Administration, DMA (15 days response time). Separately, under the Odisha Right to Public Services (ORTPS) Act 2012, a citizen may appeal to the service's Appellate Authority within 30-90 days of the decision (the Appellate Authority must dispose of the appeal within 30 days), and may further appeal to the Revisional Authority within 30-90 days of the Appellate Authority's order (no statutory disposal deadline applies to the Revisional Authority).
escalation_authority: Designated officer: Sanitary Inspector (concerned ward). Appellate Authority: City Health Officer. Revisional Authority: Municipal Commissioner.

faq.question: What information do I need to give when reporting uncollected garbage?
faq.answer: Your locality/ward and a phone number where you can be reached -- these are required to register and track the complaint.

faq.question: How long should it take for the waste to be lifted after I complain?
faq.answer: Per the HUDD Citizen's Charter, the process time limit for this service is 3 days.

faq.question: Is there a fee for reporting uncollected waste?
faq.answer: No. The HUDD Citizen's Charter states 'No fees' for this service.

citizen_guidance: Keep your acknowledgement receipt/complaint number -- it is needed to track status and to escalate if the 3-day limit is not met.

sub_service: Permission to cut a municipal road (e.g. for utility or pipeline work)
problem_type: Need permission to cut a municipal road
department: Engineering section, Urban Local Body (Municipal Corporation / Municipality / NAC)
description: Citizens or contractors who need to cut a municipal road (e.g. to lay a pipeline or cable) must obtain prior permission from the concerned ULB and pay restoration charges estimated by the Junior Engineer. The restoration fee is not fixed -- it is estimated case-by-case based on the proposed type of road cutting. This is a manual-only process in the source document.
procedure: (1) Visit the concerned engineering section of the ULB. (2) Submit an application to the City Engineer stating the purpose of the road cutting, locality details, and applicant details. (3) After verification by the Junior Engineer, collect the estimate of restoration charges applicable to the case. (4) Submit the restoration fees along with the application for road cutting permission to the counter officer of the concerned section. (5) Collect the acknowledgement receipt. (6) Collect the permission letter from the concerned authority.
sla: 7 days process time limit, per the HUDD Citizen's Charter.
complaint_channel: In person at the ULB's engineering section
escalation_procedure: If the service is not delivered within the stated process time limit, escalate per HUDD's Citizen's Charter grievance escalation matrix. For Municipal Corporations: Level 1 - Additional Municipal Commissioner / Executive Officer (7 days response time); Level 2 - Municipal Commissioner (7 days response time); Level 3 - Directorate of Municipal Administration, DMA (15 days response time); Level 4 - Commissioner-cum-Secretary, Housing & Urban Development Department (30 days response time). For Municipalities/NACs: Level 1 - City Manager (7 days response time); Level 2 - Section Head (7 days response time); Level 3 - Executive Officer (7 days response time); Level 4 - Directorate of Municipal Administration, DMA (15 days response time). Separately, under the Odisha Right to Public Services (ORTPS) Act 2012, a citizen may appeal to the service's Appellate Authority within 30-90 days of the decision (the Appellate Authority must dispose of the appeal within 30 days), and may further appeal to the Revisional Authority within 30-90 days of the Appellate Authority's order (no statutory disposal deadline applies to the Revisional Authority).
escalation_authority: Designated officer: Concerned Junior Engineer. Appellate Authority: Executive Engineer concerned. Revisional Authority: City Engineer.

faq.question: How much does road cutting permission cost?
faq.answer: There is no fixed fee -- the restoration charge is estimated per case by the Junior Engineer after site verification, based on the proposed type of road cutting. Budget for this before applying.

citizen_guidance: The restoration fee is not fixed -- it is estimated per case, so confirm the estimate before you pay. Retain your acknowledgement receipt and permission letter.

sub_service: Application for a new individual pipe water connection
problem_type: Need to apply for a new water supply connection to a property (not a fault on an existing connection)
department: Public Health Engineering Organization (PHEO), Housing & Urban Development Department, Government of Odisha
description: Citizens can apply for a new individual pipe water connection to their property, either online via the ULB portal or manually at the PHEO office. This is a distinct service from reporting a leak or fault on an already-existing connection (see WATER_WS_PIPELINE_REPAIR) -- it is the application process for a first-time connection. Sourced from the HUD Citizen's Charter's detailed services table (service #14, 'Pipe water connection'), a separate, more granular table than the one used for this project's other Odisha records.
procedure: Online: (1) Visit www.ulbodisha.gov.in and select the applicable municipal corporation/municipality. (2) Go to 'citizen services' and select 'Water Connection & Charges'. (3) Click 'Online Application for new connection', complete the application form, and submit. (4) Collect the acknowledgement receipt. Manual: (1) Deposit the filled-in application form at the maintenance division/sub-division of the Public Health department, along with the security fee. (2) After the plan is verified by the concerned division, deposit the requisite scrutiny fee and collect the acknowledgement receipt from the cash counter. (3) Collect the sanctioned letter from the respective maintenance division/sub-division.
required_documents: Online application: Patta / pauti / kabala / Holding receipt; Agreement between the applicant and PHEO on Rs. 10 non-judicial stamp paper (available at PHEO)

Manual application: A set of blueprint plans (in duplicate); Holding number; Layout of the premises; Proposed point of connection; Fixtures and future extension details, if any; Details of the licensed plumber or contractor
sla: 45 days process time limit, per the HUDD Citizen's Charter's detailed services table (service #14).
complaint_channel: Online: www.ulbodisha.gov.in, under 'citizen services' > 'Water Connection & Charges'
Manual: maintenance division / sub-division of the Public Health department
contact_information: Concerned Junior Engineer at the PHEO maintenance division/sub-division; exact contact varies by ULB and is not individually listed in the source document.
escalation_procedure: Per the HUDD Citizen's Charter's detailed services table for this specific service: Designated Officer -> concerned Junior Engineer; Appellate Authority -> concerned Assistant Engineer; Revisional Authority -> concerned Executive Engineer.
escalation_authority: Designated officer: Junior Engineer (concerned). Appellate Authority: Assistant Engineer (concerned). Revisional Authority: Executive Engineer (concerned).

faq.question: How much does a new water connection cost in Odisha?
faq.answer: A fixed Security Fee of Rs. 60 applies, per the HUDD Citizen's Charter. A separate Scrutiny Fee also applies, but its amount is not fixed in the source -- it states the fee 'as applicable for the type of connection', so the exact figure isn't available without checking with the PHEO office.

faq.question: How long does a new water connection take in Odisha?
faq.answer: The stated process time limit is 45 days.

faq.question: Can I apply online for a new water connection in Odisha?
faq.answer: Yes -- via www.ulbodisha.gov.in, under 'citizen services' > 'Water Connection & Charges' > 'Online Application for new connection'. A manual (in-person) application path is also available at the PHEO office.

citizen_guidance: The Security Fee (Rs. 60) is fixed, but the Scrutiny Fee varies by connection type and is not stated as a fixed figure in the source -- confirm the exact scrutiny fee with the PHEO office before applying.
